problem:
The system of equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}3x-4y+z=2 \\ x-6y+11z=3 \\ 3x-4y-z=4\end{aligned}
$$

can be represented using matrix notation as

$$
[\begin{aligned}3 & -4 & a \\ 1 & b & c \\ 3 & -4 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3 \\ 4\end{aligned}].
$$

What are the values of $a,b$ and $c?$

activity_context.topic_title: Representing 3x3 Systems of Equations Using a Matrix Product

feedback.problem:
The system of equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}-3x+y+7z=5 \\ x-4y+8z=1 \\ -6y+9z=2\end{aligned}
$$

can be represented using matrix notation as

$$
[\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 & 7 \\ 1 & -4 & b \\ 0 & a & 9\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}c \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

What are the values of $a,b,$ and $c?$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, let's write the system so that $x$, $y$, and $z$ appear in each equation:

$$
{\begin{aligned}-3x+y+7z=5 \\ x-4y+8z=1 \\ 0x-6y+9z=2\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can write the system in the form $Ax=b,$ where

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 & 7 \\ 1 & -4 & 8 \\ 0 & -6 & 9\end{aligned}]
$$

is the coefficient matrix,

$$
b=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]
$$

is the column vector of constants, and

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]
$$

is the column vector of variables.

So, the equation $Ax=b$ becomes

$$
[\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 & 7 \\ 1 & -4 & 8 \\ 0 & -6 & 9\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, $a=-6,\,b=8,\,c=5.$
